existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect` is absent as an R6 resource and appears to have been merged into `ClinicalUseDefinition`. Top concerns are resource identity breakage, required `type` and `subject`, moved fields under `undesirableEffect`, and conversion of `Population` to `Reference(Group)`. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official cross-version diff or ConceptMap.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a field-by-field rename only. R4 data must be transformed into `ClinicalUseDefinition`, set `type` to `undesirable-effect`, move effect details under the `undesirableEffect` backbone, convert subject references to R6 target choices, and decide how to represent population and status. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for new target types, `CodeableReference.reference`, `status`, `management`, `library`, and other added elements.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the computable changes because the R6 package index lacks the assigned StructureDefinition and the R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` snapshot contains the undesirable-effect backbone and discriminator constraints. Confidence is lower for committee intent and preferred migration mechanics because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative change note was available locally.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductUndesirableEffect has a resource-identity break: R4 resource identity is absent in R6 and appears merged into ClinicalUseDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 96/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
